title: Resource extraction job transactional enqueue and idempotency plan
description: Documents the atomicity and replay-safety invariants introduced by 20260817120000_resource_extraction_jobs_transactional_enqueue.sql, satisfying ENG-154/AD-27 (transactional outbox for this worker flow) and ENG-139 (idempotency key, safe replay).

mechanism.fires_on: public.resource_ingestion_jobs AFTER UPDATE WHEN new.status = 'succeeded' AND old.status IS DISTINCT FROM 'succeeded'

execution_note: This plan is a reviewed specification artifact, not an executable harness. Verifying live-transaction atomicity and concurrent-insert convergence requires a running Postgres/Supabase instance, which was not available in the session that authored this migration. The cases below must be executed against a real database (e.g. via a pgTAP suite or an integration test with db:ready) before this plan can be marked as run, not merely documented.

atomicity_cases.name: extraction job exists immediately after ingestion job succeeds, in the same transaction
atomicity_cases.setup: claim a queued resource_ingestion_jobs row, then call completeResourceIngestionJob for it
atomicity_cases.expected: exactly one resource_extraction_jobs row exists for that student/resource/strategy pair once the UPDATE commits, because the trigger runs inside the same statement's transaction

atomicity_cases.name: a rolled-back ingestion completion never leaves an orphaned extraction job
atomicity_cases.setup: begin a transaction, update resource_ingestion_jobs.status to succeeded, then roll back instead of committing
atomicity_cases.expected: no resource_extraction_jobs row exists after rollback, because trigger effects are part of the same transaction and roll back with it

idempotency_cases.name: replaying the ingestion validation handler does not create a duplicate extraction job
idempotency_cases.setup: claim and process a resource_ingestion_jobs row to completion (extraction job created), then simulate a stale-claim reclaim and re-run the handler for a row that somehow re-reaches the succeeded transition for the same logical identity
idempotency_cases.expected: the second insert attempt hits resource_extraction_jobs_logical_identity_uniq and is silently skipped (ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING); exactly one row remains

idempotency_cases.name: completeResourceIngestionJob is itself single-fire per job
idempotency_cases.setup: call completeResourceIngestionJob twice for the same jobId/workerId after the first call already transitioned status away from claimed
idempotency_cases.expected: the second call's WHERE .eq('status','claimed') matches zero rows, so the UPDATE (and therefore the trigger) never fires a second time for that job

concurrency_cases.name: two concurrent transactions racing to create the extraction job for the same logical identity converge to one row
concurrency_cases.setup: two sessions concurrently execute an UPDATE that satisfies the trigger's WHEN clause for the same student_id, resource_id, extraction_strategy_version, chunking_strategy_version
concurrency_cases.expected: the unique index resource_extraction_jobs_logical_identity_uniq allows only one INSERT to commit; the second, losing transaction's trigger-driven INSERT hits ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING and commits with zero new rows, never erroring and never duplicating

regression_cases.name: RLS negative-authorization plan still passes
regression_cases.result: 10 plans, 90 cases, all passing, including resource-extraction-jobs.rls-plan.json (5 cases)

regression_cases.name: extraction quality eval gate still passes
